scope: Documented PostgreSQL 17 counter-lifetime feasibility boundary; no native runtime experiment or universal SQL impossibility proof
requiredInvariant: Spent work cannot be refunded by savepoint/statement rollback; retained occupancy and unresolved reservations remain distinct.

findings.mechanism: transactional table counters inside protected work block
findings.reason: Caught exception rolls back persistent database changes in the block; counter increments can disappear with failed effects.
Documented preservation within the catching function is not persistent protected account state across later calls/adopted host savepoints.

findings.result: candidate primitive, not complete account design
findings.reason: nextval is not reclaimed on abort, but state may revert after crash before commit. Original account association, exact charging, concurrency, privilege/reset protection and unresolved recovery still need design.

managedConstraint: No custom module allowed unless it ships with RDS PostgreSQL, Aurora PostgreSQL and Lakebase; no eligible common callback module identified.
nextDesignProofs: define each required account lifetime explicitly: call, operation, adopted transaction and recovery
prove nonrefundable charges across nested exceptions and host savepoint rollback
preserve protected original identity and authority across pooled/adopted calls
admit native materialization and recovery bounds before effects
qualify exact provider/version privileges and crash/failover subset
